quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

36 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A sharp right turn is ahead.
A road joins from the right.
The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the road will turn sharply right and then sharply left.

questions.question: What can you do when driving on a highway next to a single broken white line?

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate lanes going in the same direction. You may cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: While in a car on a highway, what is the law about alcohol?

options.text: It is illegal to drink from or have open alcohol containers in the car.
It is legal to drink alcohol if you are not driving.
It is legal to drink alcohol while driving if you are not drunk.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is illegal to drink from or have open alcohol containers in the car.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive under the influence of alcohol. Neither drivers nor passengers can have open alcohol containers in a car that is running.

questions.question: After passing another car, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the car over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can return to your original lane when you see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spots before moving back.

questions.question: You are in a minor car accident with no injuries and little damage. What should you do?

options.text: Leave your car in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your car out of the traffic lane, if possible.
Do not move your car for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your car out of the traffic lane, if possible.
questions.explanation: After an accident with no injuries, move your car out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.

questions.question: When may you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve.
On a road with a solid line next to your lane.
On a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means you may cross to change lanes. Only pass when it is safe. Do not pass on hills, curves, or where solid lines are marked.

questions.question: When turning left from a one-way street with multiple lanes onto a two-way street, which lane should you start in?

options.text: The far left lane.
Any available lane.
The lane closest to the middle of the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: The far left lane.
questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from a one-way street in the far left lane.

questions.question: A car coming toward you has its high beams on at night, making it hard to see. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at the bright headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the other car from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: A yellow traffic light warns that red is coming. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, what should you do?

options.text: Stop.
Continue and clear the intersection safely.
Speed up to avoid an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue and clear the intersection safely.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, continue through and clear the intersection as quickly as you can.

questions.question: What must you do at an intersection with a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Wait for the green light before going.
Slow down and cross carefully.
Stop before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be cautious. Stay alert for crossing traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?

options.text: In an intersection with no oncoming cars.
Wherever signs and road markings allow passing.
In a curve with no oncoming cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever signs and road markings allow passing.
questions.explanation: Never pass in intersections, curves, or hills. Only pass where signs and road markings permit it, and only if you have enough space to do so safely.

questions.question: What is the purpose of work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs?

options.text: To make drivers angry about slow traffic.
To inconvenience drivers.
To keep traffic away from dangerous work zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep traffic away from dangerous work zones.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for workers and drivers. Watch for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests.

questions.question: Which traffic lights always require you to stop?

options.text: Solid red, flashing red, and blacked out signals.
Solid red, red arrows, and flashing yellow.
Solid red, flashing red, and yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Solid red, flashing red, and blacked out signals.
questions.explanation: You must stop at solid red lights, flashing red lights, and signals that are blacked out. Yellow means the light is about to turn red; stop if you can do so safely. Flashing yellow means proceed with caution.

questions.question: Your car breaks down. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and move into the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.
Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: When your car breaks down, turn on your hazard lights and get off the road away from traffic if possible.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Look through the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Only use your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Place your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly through the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors. Back up slowly.

questions.question: Why should you increase your following distance behind large vehicles?

options.text: To see around the sides of the vehicle.
Because other drivers will try to pass before you.
To avoid being caught in the vehicle's slipstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see around the sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles block your view of the road. Drivers of trucks, buses, and vehicles with trailers may not see you if you follow too closely. Increase your distance to see around them and see the road ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrian crossing.
Side road.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.question: You see people near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Honk and keep your speed.
Speed up to clear the area quickly.
Slow down and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass carefully.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians near the road. Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Missing an exit.
Being late for an appointment.
Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue makes you less able to control your vehicle and react quickly. You could fall asleep at the wheel and crash, which could injure or kill you or others.

questions.question: You should turn on your headlights:

options.text: One half hour after sunset.
When stopped at a railroad crossing.
When parked at a school.

questions.correctAnswerText: One half hour after sunset.
questions.explanation: Use headlights from one half hour after sunset until one half hour before sunrise. Also use them when it rains or snows, or when you cannot see 1,000 feet ahead.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, you should:

options.text: Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.
Turn on your high beam headlights to better see the vehicles ahead of you.
Keep the instrument panel lights bright to be more visible to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night because you cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can stop your vehicle within the area lit by your headlights.

questions.question: It is more dangerous to drive at night than during the day because:

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
The road is always more slippery at night.
Your reaction time is slower at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
questions.explanation: At night, you have less visibility and face glare from oncoming headlights. Always use headlights and drive carefully in the dark.

questions.question: To avoid hydroplaning while driving in rainy conditions, you should:

options.text: Drive at a speed appropriate for ideal conditions.
Apply your brakes as soon as your car starts to skid.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose contact with the wet road and your vehicle slides on water. Drive slowly in rain and wet conditions to prevent this.

questions.question: Signs with orange backgrounds are:

options.text: General warning signs.
Construction and maintenance warning signs.
Regulatory signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction and maintenance warning signs.
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn you about construction and maintenance work ahead.

questions.question: A large truck is ahead of you and is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. The truck:

options.text: May complete its turn in either of the two lanes.
May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.
Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need extra space to turn because their back wheels follow a tighter path than their front wheels. The truck may need to swing into another lane to complete a right turn safely.

questions.question: When using a roundabout, drivers should:

options.text: Stop in the middle of the roundabout.
Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
Yield to entering traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: At a roundabout, yield to cars already inside the circle. Enter from the right and follow the circle until you reach your exit.

questions.question: A distraction when driving is:

options.text: Anything that causes evasive action while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your mind off driving. Distracted driving can cause crashes, injuries, and deaths.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lane markings mean that:

options.text: Neither lane may pass.
Both lanes may pass.
The lane to the right may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Neither lane may pass.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. No one may pass when you see these lines.

questions.question: Roadways are the most slippery:

options.text: During a heavy downpour.
After it has been raining for awhile.
During the first rain after a dry spell.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first rain after a dry spell.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery during the first rain after a long dry period because oil and dust on the road have not been washed away yet.

questions.question: Fines in a construction zone are:

options.text: Doubled.
Tripled.
Cut in half.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doubled.
questions.explanation: Traffic fines are doubled in construction zones where workers are present. Drive carefully and follow all signs and instructions in these areas.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you should:

options.text: Turn into any lane.
Turn into first lane.
Turn into second lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn into first lane.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the first available legal lane that matches the direction you are turning.

questions.question: When you want to change lanes, you should never:

options.text: Move into another lane while within an intersection.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into another lane while within an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes while in an intersection. Before changing lanes, always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and watch for other vehicles.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, it is safe to return to your lane if you:

options.text: Cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
Have passed the other vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Return to your lane only when the vehicle you passed is far enough behind you. When you see both headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough space to move back.

questions.question: If a road is slippery, maintain a following distance that is:

options.text: No different than normal.
Farther from the car ahead than normal.
Closer to the car ahead than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther from the car ahead than normal.
questions.explanation: You need more time and distance to stop on a slippery road. Always increase your following distance when driving on wet, icy, or snowy roads.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Increase your speed to get through the zone as quickly as possible.
Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop suddenly.
Maintain your normal speed the whole way through the zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: Slow down when entering a work zone. Obey posted speed limits and watch for workers and sudden obstacles ahead.

questions.question: When driving under snowy or icy conditions:

options.text: It is safe to use your cruise control.
Make speed and directional changes more gradually than you would otherwise.
Drive as you would under normal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make speed and directional changes more gradually than you would otherwise.
questions.explanation: On snow or ice, make all speed and direction changes slowly. Never use cruise control in these conditions because your tires may lose grip and you could lose control.
